summary: P1 bounded Rosch pilot: finite cue validity, fixed-cue inclusion boundary, assigned category-specific cue sensitivity, and membership/typicality separation. Does not derive a basic level or model human processing.

sources.citation: Rosch (1978), Principles of Categorization. Full local 25-page reformatted chapter read; local pp.5-6 cue validity and pp.10-16 typicality. Local pages are not original chapter pp.27-48.
sources.available: Pinned local primary source; SHA-256 45e33ffdfe2d79f5c63f1d70b28bcc5c8e6e72f3b761c17930a8af4bc50d8fbe. Independent semantic review pending.

definitions_mapped.source: R2-03 local p.5: P(category | cue), restricted to finite empirical frequency and Boolean predicates; optional undefined case added.
R2-03 local pp.5-6: source sum at unit weights; generalized weights and the fixed-cue-list hypothesis are explicit added choices, not Rosch's category-specific selection rule.
Same-data normalized-frequency encoding for the conditional probability definition; finite restriction, not a full real-valued measure theory.
R2-02/R2-03 hierarchy labels are source-inspired; sample, coextensive features, numerical counts and category-specific cue lists are constructed inputs.
R2-04 local pp.10-16: separate membership and ordinal goodness; finite numeric scales, direct weak ordering and ties are illustrative additions.
R2-01 cognitive economy; R2-02 empirical basic-level convergence; R2-03 feature selection; R2-04 human ratings; R2-05 mechanisms; R2-06 context; R2-07 attribute origins; R2-08 events/scripts.

theorems.name: Frequency.count_nonnegative
theorems.source_claim: Finite-frequency helper: unit-indicator counts are nonnegative.

theorems.name: Frequency.count_monotone
theorems.source_claim: Finite-frequency helper: observed inclusion implies a count inequality.

theorems.name: Frequency.joint_count_le_cue
theorems.source_claim: Intersection-count bound supporting the restricted conditional probability definition.

theorems.name: Frequency.undefined_exactly_zero_cue
theorems.source_claim: Explicit undefined-conditioning interface; zero-frequency cues are not assigned an empirical probability.

theorems.name: Frequency.positive_cue_is_defined
theorems.source_claim: Local PDF p.5: positive cue frequency makes the finite conditional-frequency value defined.

theorems.name: Frequency.cue_ratio_range
theorems.source_claim: Finite conditional frequency lies in [0,1] when the cue has positive frequency.

theorems.name: Frequency.cue_ratio_monotone
theorems.source_claim: Encoding boundary: nested categories and one fixed positive cue yield monotone conditional frequency.

theorems.name: Frequency.fixed_cue_score_monotone
theorems.source_claim: Same cue list and nonnegative weights preserve inclusion monotonicity; weights generalize the source's unweighted sum.

theorems.name: Frequency.no_strict_interior_maximum_with_fixed_cues
theorems.source_claim: A containing category cannot score strictly lower with identical admissible cues; not a refutation of Rosch's category-specific account.

theorems.name: Frequency.normalization_cancels
theorems.source_claim: Same-data representation check: conditioning normalized counts equals the direct ratio on positive denominators.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.hierarchy_and_positive_cues
theorems.source_claim: Constructed nonvacuity witness: nested kitchen-chair/chair/furniture predicates and positive shared cues.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.fixed_cues_favor_parent
theorems.source_claim: Assigned four-observation dataset: fixed cues give chair 8/3 and furniture 3; not published measurements.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.assigned_category_cues_allow_interior_maximum
theorems.source_claim: Assigned category-specific cue lists give furniture 1, chair 2, kitchen-chair 1; cue selection is input, not predicted.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.undefined_is_not_defined_zero
theorems.source_claim: Boundary case distinguishing an absent cue from a positive cue never paired with the category.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.negative_weight_breaks_monotonicity
theorems.source_claim: Counterexample to dropping nonnegative weights, not to the source's unweighted proposal.

theorems.name: ConstructedCategories.dropping_inclusion_breaks_monotonicity
theorems.source_claim: Reversed noninclusion in the constructed hierarchy invalidates the corresponding monotonicity claim.

theorems.name: Typicality.score_order_is_preorder
theorems.source_claim: Infrastructure for a restricted ordinal representation; not an empirical generalization.

theorems.name: Typicality.best_preserved_by_order
theorems.source_claim: Same membership and equivalent order on members preserve best-member status.

theorems.name: Typicality.positive_affine_rescaling_preserves_order
theorems.source_claim: Ordinal representation check; does not preserve or claim meaningful cardinal distances.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.ordinal_matches_scores
theorems.source_claim: A directly specified weak ordering matches the assigned numeric scores on all four constructed items.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.members_can_differ_in_typicality
theorems.source_claim: Local PDF pp.10-16 motivates unequal goodness among members; the numerical scores are constructed inputs.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.tied_best_members
theorems.source_claim: Constructed robin/sparrow tie demonstrates compatibility with more than one best member; the tie is not a source measurement.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.no_unique_best_member
theorems.source_claim: Nonuniqueness follows in this explicit tied-ranking example; not a universal claim about all category maxima.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.rescaling_preserves_best
theorems.source_claim: Direct ordering and rescaled scores select the same best members in this finite example.

theorems.name: Typicality.ConstructedBirds.ranking_does_not_determine_membership
theorems.source_claim: Unconstrained membership can vary while ranking is held fixed; a logical separation illustration, not a competing empirical bird classification.

inventory_dispositions.scope: No cognitive-economy objective or empirical perceived-world account.
Constructed nested category predicates only; no basic-level selection, four-measure convergence, knowledge-dependent prediction or branchwise cut theorem.
Finite conditional-frequency definition and encoding boundary checked; assigned cue-list sensitivity is illustrative. No derived feature selection or empirical/basic-level maximum claim established.
Membership/rank separation, differing member typicalities and tied maxima on assigned data; limited ordinal representation correspondence. No human-judgment validation.
No pair of processing/representation/learning mechanisms fitted to the source evidence.
No context dynamics or prediction of context-dependent category judgments.
Cue lists are explicit inputs, not a theory of culturally/category-dependent attribute formation.
No event/script hierarchy, memory or comprehension model.

encoding_checks.frequency_normalization: Proved equality on the same finite sample with positive denominators.
encoding_checks.ordinal_representation: Proved direct-order/score correspondence on constructed example and best-member invariance under order preservation.
encoding_checks.scope: Limited representation checks, not independent semantic validation or robustness of the entire theory.
encoding_checks.category_specific_cues: Semantic sensitivity with changed cue lists, not representation-preserving robustness.

evidence: Source-linked bounded construction and explicit source-to-code limitations; self-assessment, not independent review.
simplifications: Finite uniform observation frequencies and Boolean event predicates replace general probabilities.
Natural-number scores represent one finite weak ordering; no cardinal psychological scale.
omissions: R2-01: No cognitive-economy objective or empirical perceived-world account.
R2-05: No pair of processing/representation/learning mechanisms fitted to the source evidence.
R2-06: No context dynamics or prediction of context-dependent category judgments.
R2-07: Cue lists are explicit inputs, not a theory of culturally/category-dependent attribute formation.
R2-08: No event/script hierarchy, memory or comprehension model.
No empirical basic-level or prototype-effect validation; no cue-learning rule.
additions: Nonnegative weighted sum generalizes the unit-weight source sum.
Category-specific feature lists, numeric frequency data and rank ties are assigned.
Zero-frequency cues use an explicit option interface; raw rational division is internal.
The non-entailment countermodel's alternative membership is not an empirical bird model.

determination_rationale: R2-03 and R2-04 fragments only. This attempt does not show whole-source as-is transfer, necessary restructuring, or impossibility. Keep all eight inventory dispositions visible.
